# Hiring From Tier 2 and Tier 3 Cities in India? Background Verification Is No Longer Optional


September 18, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/hiring-from-tier-2-and-tier-3-cities-in-india-background-verification-is-no-longer-optional/#respond)


Something significant is happening in Indian hiring that most founders and HR leaders have not fully processed yet.


The talent map has shifted. Companies that once hired exclusively from Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, and Hyderabad are now actively recruiting from Jaipur, Indore, Lucknow, Coimbatore, Bhubaneswar, and dozens of other cities that were barely on the hiring radar five years ago. Remote work made this possible. Cost advantages made it attractive. And the depth of talent in these cities made it sustainable.


But here is the part nobody is talking about loudly enough. As hiring expands into tier 2 and tier 3 cities, so does hiring fraud. And the data from 2026 makes this impossible to dismiss.


## The Fraud Data That Should Worry You


According to a major annual fraud report published earlier this year, high risk employee fraud zones in India doubled from 5 cities in 2024 to 10 cities in 2025. The most striking part of that finding is where the new additions came from. They were not more metros. They were tier 2 and tier 3 cities.


This shift makes sense when you think about it. In metro cities, professional networks are dense. Someone on your team might know someone at the candidate’s previous employer. Industry circles overlap. Informal verification happens naturally through shared connections.


In tier 2 and tier 3 cities, those networks are thinner. The candidate’s previous employers might be local businesses that do not have a formal HR department. The educational institutions on their resume might be ones you have never heard of. The professional references they provide might be people you have no way of independently validating.


None of this means candidates from smaller cities are less trustworthy. The vast majority are genuine, talented, and exactly who they claim to be. But the absence of informal verification networks means that when fraud does occur, it is harder to catch through traditional methods. And the data tells us that fraud is increasingly occurring in exactly these geographies.


## Why Traditional Verification Fails Outside Metros


The traditional model of[background verification](https://compose1.com/verify/) was built around metro hiring realities. Agencies had offices in major cities. Their field agents could physically visit addresses and employer offices in Bangalore or Mumbai within a day. University verification was faster because the institutions were well known and had established processes for handling verification requests.


Scale that model to a candidate from a tier 3 city, and every step becomes harder. The agency may not have local coverage. Physical address visits take longer and cost more. Previous employers may be small firms without a dedicated HR team to respond to verification requests. Educational institutions may have limited administrative infrastructure for processing external queries.


The result is predictable: longer turnaround times, higher costs, and lower reliability. For companies that are hiring from smaller cities specifically because of cost and speed advantages, paying premium prices for slow, uncertain verification defeats the purpose.


This is exactly why the shift to digital, government database based verification matters so much for non metro hiring. Government databases do not care whether the candidate is from Mumbai or Muzaffarpur. A PAN number verified against the Income Tax Department returns the same authoritative data regardless of geography. An EPFO record queried through a UAN returns the same employment history whether the employer was a Bangalore tech company or a Lucknow manufacturing firm.

The reason[Compose1](https://compose1.com/) Verify works so well for companies hiring beyond metros is that it was built to be entirely geography independent. There are no field agents, no local offices, and no physical visits. Everything runs through direct API connections to government databases.


When you run a verification, it does not matter where the candidate lives, where they previously worked, or where their documents were issued. All from a browser, all in seconds, all returning the same quality of authoritative government data regardless of location.


For a company in Bangalore hiring a customer support team in Jaipur, or a Delhi based startup building an operations team in Bhubaneswar, or a fully remote company with employees scattered across fifteen cities, this location independence is not a convenience. It is a necessity.


The cross record identity matching adds another layer of value specifically for non metro hiring. When you cannot rely on shared professional networks to informally validate a candidate’s identity, having four independent government databases all confirming the same name and date of birth gives you a level of confidence that no personal reference from an unfamiliar city could match.


## The Business Case for Verifying Every Non Metro Hire


Let me put this in practical terms. When you hire from a metro city, the informal safety nets are imperfect but they exist. Industry connections, well known employer brands, recognisable educational institutions, and dense professional networks all provide ambient verification signals.


When you hire from a tier 2 or tier 3 city, many of those signals are absent. The employer names on the resume might be unfamiliar. The institutions might be ones you cannot evaluate by reputation alone. The references might be people outside your professional orbit.


This does not mean the candidates are riskier. It means you have less ambient information to work with, which makes formal verification more important, not less.


Running PAN, UAN, Voter ID, and Driving Licence checks through Compose1 replaces those missing ambient signals with something much stronger: verified government data. It takes the same amount of time regardless of the candidate’s location. It costs the same regardless of geography. And it returns the same authoritative results whether the candidate is from Chennai or Chandigarh.


## A Simple Rule for Non Metro Hiring


If you are expanding your hiring beyond the top six or seven metro cities, adopt one simple rule: verify every candidate through government databases before extending an offer. No exceptions based on role level. No exceptions based on how good the interview felt. No exceptions because “they seem genuine.”


Make PAN and UAN verification the minimum for every hire. These two checks confirm identity and employment history, which are the two areas most vulnerable to fraud in non metro hiring. Add Voter ID and Driving Licence for a complete cross referenced profile when the role warrants additional confidence.


The best employee background verification tool for non metro hiring is one that does not depend on local infrastructure, physical visits, or agency coverage maps. Compose1 Verify runs on government data that exists for every formal employee in India, regardless of which city they call home.


## The Opportunity Is Real. Protect It.


Hiring from tier 2 and tier 3 cities is one of the smartest strategic moves a growing Indian company can make in 2026. The talent is strong. The costs are lower. The candidates are hungry for opportunity.


But expanding your talent map without expanding your verification process creates a gap that fraudulent candidates will eventually exploit. The fraud data from 2025 and 2026 proves that this is already happening.


Close the gap before it costs you. Verify every non metro hire with the same rigour you would apply to a metro candidate. With Compose1 Verify, that rigour takes seconds and costs a fraction of what a single bad hire would set you back.


Your next great team member might be in Indore. Make sure their resume is as real as their talent.
